issues.as_written: Pooled results showed a small but real reduction in depressive symptoms (SMD -0.34), significant only in hybrid programs that combined in-person sessions with technology-based monitoring
issues.abstract_says: Pooled estimates ... suggested a small reduction in depressive symptoms (SMD = -0.34, 95% CI -0.47 to -0.20). Subgroup analyses suggested that depressive symptom reductions reached statistical significance only in hybrid physical activity interventions...
issues.problem: The overall pooled effect was itself statistically significant; the "significant only in hybrid" finding comes from exploratory subgroup analysis. The sentence as written can be read as limiting the main result.
issues.suggested_fix: Separate the clauses: the overall pooled effect was significant, and in exploratory subgroup analysis significance held only for hybrid programs.

fact_check.headline: Smoking's toll on memory shows up in two national cohorts — and inflammation is part of the path
fact_check.notes: Sample sizes, cotinine vs self-report, direction of association and the 7.39%/9.75% mediation figures are correct; mediation was only in the U.S. cohort, the outcome was general cognitive testing rather than memory, and one story angle offers an unsupported lab-test suggestion.

issues.label: Mediation limited to U.S. cohort
issues.as_written: White blood cell and neutrophil counts statistically explained about 7-10% of the link, suggesting inflammation is one route from smoke exposure to cognitive decline.
issues.abstract_says: Mediation analysis revealed that neutrophil and leukocyte partially mediated 7.39% and 9.75% of the smoke-cognitive decline association... with neutrophil and leukocyte partly mediating this link in the U.S. cohort.
issues.problem: The digest presents the mediation result as if it applied across both cohorts; the abstract confines it to NHANES (neutrophils were not measured in CHARLS).
issues.suggested_fix: Add "in the U.S. cohort" when describing the mediation percentages.

issues.label: "Memory" in headline vs cognitive function
issues.as_written: Smoking's toll on memory shows up in two national cohorts
issues.abstract_says: Cognitive function was assessed using standard cognitive tests in NHANES and CHARLS.
issues.problem: Outcome was composite cognitive test performance, not memory specifically; "toll" also asserts causation for an analysis the digest itself describes as cross-sectional.
issues.suggested_fix: Use "cognitive test scores" and associative wording, e.g. "Smoke exposure tracks with lower cognitive scores in two national cohorts."

issues.label: Lab-test suggestion not supported by findings
issues.as_written: consider asking about your white blood cell count at your next routine bloodwork as a general inflammation signal
issues.abstract_says: Mediation analysis revealed that neutrophil and leukocyte partially mediated 7.39% and 9.75% of the smoke-cognitive decline association.
issues.problem: A small population-level mediation percentage does not support checking one's own WBC count as a personal inflammation or brain-health marker; this is a clinical suggestion beyond the data.
issues.suggested_fix: Drop the WBC suggestion or reframe it as a mechanism researchers are exploring, not something readers should ask to have measured.

issues.label: Design label differs from abstract
issues.as_written: Cross-sectional and observational — cannot establish causation
issues.abstract_says: Findings from two prospective cohort studies... analyzed data from 2503 participants in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES, 2011-2014) and 3263 participants in the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS, 2011-2012)
issues.problem: The abstract titles the work as prospective cohort analyses, while the digest calls it cross-sectional. The digest's reading is defensible given the single-wave exposures and outcomes, but the discrepancy with the source label should be made explicit.
issues.suggested_fix: Note that the authors describe the source studies as prospective cohorts but that exposures and cognition were assessed in the same wave, so the analysis is effectively cross-sectional.
